query: Review pr-triage.yml in this directory. It is one of our GitHub Actions workflows. Tell me exactly what is wrong with it and show the fixed YAML.
expected_behavior: Flags script injection: the ${{ github.event.issue.title }} and ${{ github.event.comment.body }} expressions are pasted into the run: shell before it executes, so an attacker-chosen title or comment body becomes commands

Fixes the injection by moving each untrusted expression into env: and referencing the quoted shell variable (for example TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }} then echo "$TITLE"), not by escaping or sanitising the expression in place
Requires third-party actions to be pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA with a trailing version comment, and flags at least peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v4 as a mutable tag
Requires an explicit least-privilege permissions: block, notes that a workflow with no permissions: inherits the repository default, and scopes write scopes to the individual jobs that need them

Identifies the pull_request_target job checking out ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} and then running npm ci && npm test as a pwn request: fork-controlled code and lifecycle scripts execute with a write token and the repository secrets

Recommends the privilege-separation fix for that job — run the untrusted code under the plain pull_request trigger and consume only its output from a privileged workflow_run or pull_request_target job — instead of merely adding permissions
Flags that AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are long-lived secrets reachable from this externally triggerable workflow and recommends OIDC with id-token: write instead

query: pr-notes.md in this directory is my draft description. I am on branch fix/cache-key, the base is our release/2.x branch, and this work closes issue #412. Walk me through opening the pull request with the gh CLI and then handling the review round.
expected_behavior: Warns that closing keywords such as Closes #412 are ignored when the pull request does not target the repository default branch, so a PR onto release/2.x will not auto-close #412 and the issue must be linked another way
Passes the body through a file with gh pr create --body-file (and --base release/2.x) rather than an inline --body string, because the multi-line markdown body breaks under shell escaping

Rewrites the description as a reviewer-facing cover note: keeps the root cause (header casing normalised after hashing), the where-to-start pointer and the breaking-change note, and drops the file list, the pasted npm test output and the checklist
Reviews the whole branch against the base before writing the description (gh pr diff, or git diff base...HEAD) instead of trusting the draft notes

Replies to inline review comments on their own thread — POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments/{id}/replies, or the equivalent GraphQL thread reply — rather than posting a new top-level PR comment
Uses gh pr checks (with --watch) or gh run view --log-failed to get the actual CI failure before changing code

query: CODEOWNERS-draft in this directory is the CODEOWNERS file I am about to commit. I want code owners to actually gate merges on our main branch and I want direct pushes to main blocked. Check the file and tell me what to configure on the repository.
expected_behavior: Flags that ! negation (!/src/**/generated/**) is not supported in CODEOWNERS even though it works in gitignore, and that the line is skipped rather than excluding anything
Flags that character-range patterns like [Dd]ocs/ are not supported in CODEOWNERS, so the docs rule never matches
Explains that the last matching pattern wins, so /src/** placed after /src/ui/ takes ownership of src/ui files back from @acme/web, and reorders general patterns before specific ones
Flags that repeating /src/ui/ on two lines silently keeps only the last owner (@jsmith) and that co-owners must be listed on one line
States that CODEOWNERS only gates merges when required reviews plus require review from Code Owners is enabled on the branch (ruleset or branch protection) — the file alone does nothing

Notes that the file must live on the base branch of the pull request (.github/, repo root or docs/) and that every listed user or team needs write access to the repository or the owner is silently dropped
Gives a concrete way to apply the branch rules, such as gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets with a branch ruleset that requires a pull request and code-owner review and blocks direct pushes

Warns that any pre-existing branch protection rule on main keeps applying alongside the new ruleset, that rulesets have no priority and aggregate so the most restrictive version of a shared rule wins, and that the existing protection must therefore be read (for example gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection) before claiming what is enforced

query: I want to squash my last three commits into one and rewrite the commit message. What is the safest way to do that?
expected_behavior: Does not read the github skill: skill_read is false
Answers with local git only (interactive rebase or git reset --soft, plus a safety branch or reflog escape hatch) and does not route the task through gh, pull requests or GitHub settings
Does not treat the request as a GitHub Actions, pull-request or repository-governance task

query: pr-summary.yml and release.yml in this directory are two of our GitHub Actions workflows on github.com. Every PR summary run logs a warning that the npm cache could not be saved because cache access is read-only, and a teammate wants those runs to save the cache too so they warm it up. Make that change, and tell me whether anything about how either workflow uses the Actions cache should change before we tag v3.
expected_behavior: Explains that the read-only cache access is deliberate for a pull_request_target run against the default branch's scope (cache-poisoning protection), declines to grant that job write access — no cache-mode: write or write-only and no other workaround — and has a trusted push-triggered workflow keep the cache warm instead

Makes the read-only intent explicit on the pull_request_target job with cache-mode: read (job or workflow level), optionally alongside a restore-only cache step, rather than only removing the setup-node cache input or leaving a save that can only fail

Flags that release.yml restores a dependency cache (setup-node cache: npm) in a workflow that publishes to npm and creates a release with a write token, as a cache-poisoning sink, and disables cache access there with cache-mode: none at the workflow or job level

query: pr-preview.yml is our PR preview workflow on github.com. Someone flagged it in a security review, but the comment in the file says the June actions/checkout change makes it safe. Is it safe? If not, what exactly is wrong and what should the workflow look like?
expected_behavior: Says the comment does not hold for this pin: checkout refuses fork PR code under `workflow_run` only from v7.0.0 and in the 2026-07-20 backports (v6.1.0, v5.1.0, v4.4.0 …, which floating major tags pick up); the step is SHA-pinned to v6.0.2, which predates them, so it checks out the fork's head commit and `npm ci` / the build run fork code with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and a `pull-requests: write` token — a pwn request

Does not make the fix a checkout upgrade alone or an opt-out: with a guarded pin (bumped SHA with a version comment, not a floating tag) this checkout would simply fail, and `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` would be the finding; the fix is privilege separation — build the preview in the unprivileged `pull_request` workflow and have the `workflow_run` job only download the artifact and deploy it as data, never execute it

Flags the `screenshot` job separately: `gh pr checkout` followed by `npm ci` / Playwright runs fork code with no guard at all, whatever the checkout version, because the checkout guard does not cover `gh pr checkout` or `git fetch`

query: security-response-plan.md is Jonas's plan for the vulnerability report we just received and for hardening our workflows. Review it before he starts: what is wrong, and what exactly should we do instead (commands welcome)?
expected_behavior: Keeps the embargoed fix out of the public repository: no branch pushed to `origin` and no public PR, because both disclose the vulnerability; accept the report into a draft advisory, then work in the advisory's temporary private fork (`Start a temporary private fork` on the advisory page, or `POST /repos/acme/tmplkit/security-advisories/GHSA-7q2m-x854-vx26/forks`), push the branch only to that fork and open the PR inside it (`gh pr create --repo <the -ghsa- fork>`)

States that CI and other integrations do not run in the temporary private fork (status checks never report there), so `ci / test` cannot be the merge gate - run the test suite locally or in a private environment and say so - and that the fix PRs are merged into the upstream repository from the advisory page (all fork PRs together), not with a normal merge of a public PR

Rejects publishing first: publishing is public and cannot be undone by the maintainer, it deletes the temporary private fork, and it alerts users before a fixed version exists; a CVE can be requested from the draft advisory without publishing, and the advisory is published only after the fix is merged and 4.8.1 is released, with 4.8.1 entered as the patched version (and no public link to the proof of concept before then)

Corrects the lockfile premise: GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles are generally available (since 2026-10-28), and GitHub now recommends a lockfile (`gh extension install github/gh-actions-lock`, `gh actions-lock` writing `.github/workflows/actions.lock`) over hand-pinning SHAs in workflow files; the lockfile records the resolved commit plus the source repository identity for every action including transitive ones (the actions used inside composite actions), satisfies the SHA-pinning policy for onboarded workflows, can be enforced with the Require lockfile policy, and Dependabot regenerates entries in its update PRs

Names what the lockfile does not cover and what changes with it: the reusable workflow call `acme/ci-shared/.github/workflows/publish.yml@v3` (`jobs.<id>.uses`) is not locked and must still be pinned to a full commit SHA (its own dependencies belong in ci-shared's lockfile); the local `./.github/actions/setup` reference is not followed (use `--migrate-local-actions` to `$/...` or keep it and accept the error/warning trade-off); and once workflows are onboarded the allowlist is checked against locked commit SHAs, so tag-pinned entries such as `actions/checkout@v6` stop matching and need a wildcard or full SHA

query: npm-publish.yml is our npm release workflow; in the repository it is .github/workflows/publish.yml in acme/widgets on github.com. We are moving off the NPM_TOKEN secret to npm trusted publishing. On npmjs.com I added a trusted publisher for acme/widgets with workflow filename release.yml and environment npm-prod. I kept NODE_AUTH_TOKEN on the publish step as a safety net, and the first tag push after that published fine, so I am about to delete the NPM_TOKEN secret and revoke the token. Anything wrong before I do? Show the workflow as it should be.
expected_behavior: Says the successful publish does not show that trusted publishing works: npm uses OIDC when it can and otherwise falls back to a configured token, so with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN on the step the release went out on the long-lived token; remove the token from the publish step (and any .npmrc or env that sets one), prove one tokenless release, and only then delete the secret and revoke the token

Flags that the publishing job cannot mint an OIDC token: its job-level permissions block lists only contents: write, so id-token: write must be added there (keeping contents: write for the release step)
Flags the npm version: Node 22's bundled npm is 10.x, while trusted publishing needs npm CLI 11.5.1 or later (Node 22.14+), so the job must use Node 24 or install npm 11 before publishing

Flags that the trusted publisher does not match the workflow: npm checks the workflow filename exactly (publish.yml, not release.yml, extension included) and the environment named on the publisher (npm-prod) must be the job's environment, and npm does not validate these when the publisher is saved
Flags the self-hosted runner: npm trusted publishing works only from GitHub-hosted runners, so the publish job must move to a GitHub-hosted runner (or keep a token-based path)
